opener: Hello {you}. This is a procedural request. I need a second moderator for a ruling. You are the only member who has never received a warning, which makes you neutral. (Do not read into that. It is a compliment.)

Case 117. BANANA_PHONE, 3:41 AM, the wall of a new member (kyles_lil_bro, age 11, on his brother's account, which is a separate matter under Rule 9b). Entire post: 'WELCOME!!! YOU ARE NOW MY FRIEND!!! DO YOU LIKE BANANAS!!!' Rule 2 prohibits all caps. Rule 12 requires kindness to new members. They collide. In three years I have never had two rules collide.

Todd has agreed to lunch Friday. His words: 'show me how you handle a hard call, buddy!' This is the hard call. I have the fourth draft in my bag and a sandwich. Please advise. You have eleven minutes. I have to change a filter.

choices.say: rule 12 has no exceptions. you wrote it that way on purpose. dismiss it.
read me both rules out loud. i want to hear which one blinks first.
put banana on trial. a real one, with a jury. let todd watch.

them: Rule 12 has no clauses. I wrote it that way deliberately. But dismissing 117 sets a precedent. Banana will cite it in the next 114 posts. Rule 2 becomes decoration.
There is also the matter of Todd. If I bend a rule on a case he assigned, is it bending, if the rule was written to be bent by exactly one other rule?

choices.say: the precedent is 'be kind.' best precedent you'll ever set. write it down as Rule 2d.
ask Kyle. he's the actual new member. he was on the receiving end.

them: Rule 2: No all caps. Four sub-clauses. Rule 12: Be kind to new members. Zero sub-clauses. By my own drafting, 12 outranks 2. But I did not write 'outranks.' I wrote 'no exceptions.' Are those the same? I have been on that question since 3:41.
Gary would say they are different. Gary would be right under [1.4a]. I have never wanted Gary to be wrong more.

choices.say: they're the same. 'no exceptions' is 'outranks' with its shoes off.
then the rulebook has a gap. every case needs a complainant. go find out what Kyle thinks.
ask gary. he's the only person who's read your rules more carefully than you.

them: A TRIAL. {you}. I have a script. I have had one since June. I do not have a gavel. I have a ladle. A jury of twelve requires twelve. I have Gary, Patrick (and his rock, who Patrick says counts as 1.5), Dave (disqualified, see: June), and Sticky, who would have to be carried.
The risk is obvious. If it goes sideways Todd sees a circus. The upside is also obvious. Todd said 'wow, thanks, Marcus' to six pages. He may enjoy a circus.

effects.text: patrick is on a JURY. dwayne is on the jury too. marcus says dwayne counts as 1.5. dwayne is doing his best

choices.say: circus is fine. todd likes circus. seat the jury, start the clock.
keep it small. one literalist, one sweetheart. gary and patrick. fair split guaranteed.

them: Rule 2d: 'All capital letters are permitted in the welcoming of new members.' Typed. Eleven words. It has never taken me less time to write a rule or longer to press Enter.
But who tells Banana. In writing. In caps? I cannot send caps. I would be violating Rule 2 in the act of amending it. Do I dismiss 117, or is dismissal the 118th warning?

choices.say: post it as a bulletin, v3.3. dismiss 117 in caps. once. 'WARNING 117 WITHDRAWN.' she'll frame it.
dismiss it quietly, in lowercase. rules don't lose authority by whispering. then go write Kyle a welcome.

them: I messaged him. Quote: 'who is the banana guy. is he in trouble. i liked it. i had 2 friends and now i have 3. also can i have cheats for halo.' I informed him cheats are off-topic. I informed him there is a search function. There isn't one. I told him gently.
{you}. He said 'now i have 3.' Three. He counted. I have told eleven thousand people to use the search function and not one of them has ever said 'three.'

effects.text: kyle is at 3 friends now. 3. one is a banana guy. he yells but its a welcome i think. theres a rules guy too. he told me about the search function. there isnt one. he was nice about it

choices.say: that's your ruling. the complainant is satisfied. dismiss it and welcome him properly.
kyle just told you the one thing the rulebook can't: it worked. do you want to be the guy who punishes that?

them: Gary replied in four minutes. Quote: 'Per [4.2b], Rule 12 is not a rule but a principle. Principles outrank rules by construction. Additionally, Rule 2's fourth sub-clause covers WALL POSTS. A welcome is a greeting. A greeting is not a wall post. I have been wrong in public four times this month and I enjoyed this one most.'
Gary has handed me a loophole. I find I do not want to use it. A loophole is the opposite of a principle.

choices.say: then don't use the loophole. Rule 12 wins on its own, no help from gary.
use both. loophole AND principle. cite everything when todd asks. belt and suspenders.

them: Jury seated. Foreman: Gary, objecting to the numbering. Patrick: present, with rock. Dave: 'objection' (no grounds, overruled). Banana, for the defense, has pleaded 'GUILTY OF LOVE' in capitals. Todd wrote 'haha is this a skit' and then 'sorry :)' and then 'is it a skit.'
Sticky is in the courtroom. I carried the 5-gallon. I did not spill. It is 41 minutes in. Kyle is in the gallery, asking if there is pizza.

choices.say: verdict by Sticky. if he flares, guilty. if he ignores it, dismissed. no appeals.
call a recess before somebody cites [4.2b]. then do the right thing without the ladle.

them: Two jurors. Gary has read Rule 2 ('four sub-clauses, none of which mention welcoming') and Patrick has read it too ('it says no capitals but its a nice kind of loud'). It is one to one. I am the deciding vote and also the judge. This is a structural problem and I would like to flag it to Todd (page 4).
Dave has filed an objection. It says 'objection.' There are no grounds. He will not elaborate.

choices.say: break the tie yourself. you're the judge. what does Rule 12 actually say?
let Sticky break it. flare means guilty. it's the fairest vote in the room.

them: I have drafted a welcome. By hand. As I do at TankTalk. 'Welcome to OurSpace, Kyle. Your page looks good. You have three friends. One yells, but he means it. If you have a fish, I have questions. If you have a question, there is no search function. Ask me. -- Marcus.' That is 53 words. At TankTalk the limit is 50.

There is also Friday. Todd will ask what I did with the hard call. I could say 'I held a trial.' I could say 'I wrote a rule.' Or I could say 'I wrote a welcome.' I do not know which is the better answer. Which is the better answer.

choices.say: 'i wrote a welcome.' rule-writers are everywhere. welcome-writers are scarce.
send the welcome, skip the application, and ask todd for the thing you actually want: to be the guy who types the welcomes.

them: Friday, 12:15. I will have the fourth draft (six pages plus an appendix, 31KB plain text) and a ham sandwich, which Dave says is the part that matters. Todd asked how I handle hard calls. I do not know what he wants. I do not know what I want.
I have wanted the title since August. I have not asked myself what I would do with it on a Tuesday. I think the hard call is not Banana. I think the hard call is what to hand him across the table.

choices.say: hand him the application. page 7 is Rule 2d. let him watch you amend a rule for a person.
hand him the sandwich and one question: 'what does OurSpace need?' then listen. don't hand over page 1.

them: Sticky has been brought forward. Banana's name was read aloud, in full, in a lowered voice. Sticky flared. At his reflection. At the lid. At the ladle. The record shows a flare. I am not certain at what.

Dave: 'guilty!' Gary: 'the record is inconclusive under [7.1].' Patrick: 'he flared because he's happy.' Todd: 'haha this is the best thing on the site.' {you}, I believe I have lost control of my own courtroom.

choices.say: let the betta decide. 'guilty by flare.' warning 117 stands. thread locked. (it won't lock.)
overrule the fish. you're the moderator. Rule 12. dismissed. then go write Kyle a welcome.

them: Posted. Warning 117: dismissed. Reason given: 'Rule 12 has no exceptions. It is the only rule that does.' I have also sent Kyle the welcome (49 words after revisions). I cut 'search function' and replaced it with 'ask me.' It is a small change. It felt like a large one.
I am going to say something off-topic and I will move it myself: thank you. You were neutral and it helped. I will see you in the replies, at a reasonable volume. Thread closed. (Open.)

them: Decided. Friday I hand him the application. Page 7 is Rule 2d, with the Banana dismissal attached as Exhibit A. I have also posted v3.3 now, so the members see the amendment before Todd does. That is called transparency. It is also called nerves.

I am going to eat the sandwich on Thursday as a test. If it is still a good sandwich, it will survive Friday. If it is not, I am bringing two. Thank you, {you}. This is, procedurally, the best hour I have had since the Mod of the Month nomination. Thread locked. (Left open for Todd.)
